overview.es:
Descubre Himachal Pradesh – La Tierra del Himalaya

Himachal Pradesh es uno de los destinos de montaña más escénicos de la India, ubicado en el Himalaya occidental. El estado es famoso por sus paisajes espectaculares, cumbres cubiertas de nieve, valles profundos, bosques de pinos y deodar, ríos, prados alpinos y asentamientos tradicionales del Himalaya.

Desde el encanto colonial de Shimla hasta los paisajes nevados de Manali, la cultura con influencia tibetana de Dharamshala, el ambiente tranquilo de Dalhousie y el patrimonio cultural de Chamba, Himachal Pradesh ofrece experiencias para todo tipo de viajeros.

Los amantes de la aventura pueden disfrutar de actividades como trekking, esquí, parapente, rafting en ríos de montaña y exploración, mientras que los viajeros culturales pueden descubrir templos antiguos, monasterios, arquitectura tradicional, ferias y gastronomía local.

Naturaleza y Paisajes

El estado alberga una impresionante variedad de paisajes del Himalaya, desde valles verdes y bosques hasta regiones montañosas de alta altitud. Ríos, cascadas, lagos y pasos de montaña complementan el carácter natural del destino.

Cultura y Patrimonio

Himachal Pradesh cuenta con un rico patrimonio cultural moldeado por las tradiciones del Himalaya, influencias hindúes y budistas y la historia colonial. Templos, monasterios, antiguas iglesias, palacios y pueblos tradicionales se encuentran en todo el estado.

  • Trekking por senderos del Himalaya
  • Rafting en ríos de montaña
  • Parapente en destinos seleccionados
  • Esquí y experiencias en la nieve
  • Camping y caminatas por la naturaleza
  • Rutas escénicas y viajes por carretera

El turismo en Himachal ofrece experiencias inolvidables durante todo el año, destacando destinos como Shimla, Dharamshala, Manali y Chamba entre sus principales atracciones.
overview.en:
Discover Himachal Pradesh – The Land of the Himalayas

Himachal Pradesh is one of India's most scenic mountain destinations, located in the western Himalayas. The state is famous for its dramatic landscapes, snow-covered peaks, deep valleys, pine and deodar forests, rivers, alpine meadows and traditional Himalayan settlements.

From the colonial charm of Shimla to the snow-covered landscapes of Manali, the Tibetan-influenced culture of Dharamshala, the peaceful surroundings of Dalhousie and the cultural heritage of Chamba, Himachal Pradesh offers experiences for different kinds of travellers.

Adventure lovers can enjoy activities such as trekking, skiing, paragliding, river rafting and mountain exploration, while cultural travellers can discover ancient temples, monasteries, traditional architecture, fairs and local cuisine.

Nature & Landscapes

The state contains a remarkable variety of Himalayan landscapes, ranging from green valleys and forests to high-altitude mountain regions. Rivers, waterfalls, lakes and mountain passes add to the natural character of the destination.

Culture & Heritage

Himachal Pradesh has a rich cultural heritage shaped by Himalayan traditions, Hindu and Buddhist influences and colonial history. Temples, monasteries, old churches, palaces and traditional villages can be found throughout the state.

Adventure Experiences

  • Trekking through Himalayan trails
  • River rafting in mountain rivers
  • Paragliding in selected destinations
  • Skiing and snow experiences
  • Camping and nature walks
  • Mountain sightseeing and road trips

Himachal Tourism describes the state as a destination suitable for different seasons and highlights destinations such as Shimla, Dharamshala, Manali and Chamba among its major attractions.

localFood.es: La gastronomía de Himachal Pradesh es reconfortante y está profundamente relacionada con el entorno montañoso. Entre sus platos tradicionales se encuentran Dham, Siddu, Chana Madra, Rajma Madra y Tudkiya Bhath. En las regiones del Himalaya también son populares platos de influencia tibetana como momos y thukpa.
localFood.en: Himachali cuisine is hearty, comforting and deeply connected to the mountain environment. Traditional dishes include Dham, Siddu, Chana Madra, Rajma Madra, Tudkiya Bhath and various local breads and lentil preparations. In the higher Himalayan regions, Tibetan-influenced dishes such as momos and thukpa are also popular. Local apples, apricots and other mountain produce add to the region's distinctive culinary character.
localFood.pt: A culinária de Himachal Pradesh é reconfortante e profundamente ligada ao ambiente montanhoso. Entre os pratos tradicionais estão Dham, Siddu, Chana Madra, Rajma Madra e Tudkiya Bhath. fullDescription.es: Shimla, antigua capital de verano de la India británica, es una de las estaciones de montaña más populares del Himalaya. Rodeada de colinas cubiertas de pinos y montañas nevadas, la ciudad combina patrimonio colonial con belleza natural. Los visitantes pueden explorar The Ridge, Mall Road, Christ Church y Viceregal Lodge, mientras que lugares cercanos como Kufri y Mashobra ofrecen experiencias de naturaleza y aventura. Shimla es ideal para parejas, familias, lunamieleros y viajeros que buscan una escapada tranquila a las montañas.
fullDescription.en: Shimla, the former summer capital of British India, is one of India's most popular Himalayan hill stations. Surrounded by pine-covered hills and snow-capped mountains, the city combines colonial heritage with scenic beauty. Visitors can explore the historic Ridge, Mall Road, Christ Church and Viceregal Lodge, while nearby destinations such as Kufri and Mashobra offer nature and adventure experiences. Shimla is ideal for couples, families, honeymooners and travellers looking for a relaxing mountain escape.

Today, Himachal's heritage continues through its temples, monasteries, festivals, architecture and traditional mountain communities.

overview.en:
Discover Uttarakhand – The Land of Mountains, Spirituality and Adventure

Uttarakhand is one of India's most diverse Himalayan destinations, offering an extraordinary combination of natural landscapes, spirituality, adventure and cultural heritage. From the peaceful foothills and sacred Ganga river to high Himalayan valleys and snow-covered peaks, the state offers experiences for different types of travellers.

The state is particularly important for pilgrimage tourism. Haridwar and Rishikesh are major spiritual destinations, while the famous Himalayan pilgrimage circuit includes Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri. Uttarakhand Tourism also promotes several spiritual, cultural and heritage circuits across the state.

Mountains and Hill Stations

Travellers looking for scenic mountain holidays can explore Mussoorie, Nainital, Almora and Auli. Nainital is centred around the beautiful Naini Lake and is surrounded by Himalayan hills, while Mussoorie is known for its mountain scenery and pleasant climate.

Adventure Tourism

Uttarakhand offers trekking, river rafting, skiing, camping, mountain biking, rock climbing and other outdoor experiences. Rishikesh is particularly known for river rafting and adventure activities, while Auli is one of India's important skiing destinations.

Wildlife and Nature

Wildlife enthusiasts can explore destinations such as Jim Corbett National Park, Rajaji National Park and several wildlife sanctuaries. Jim Corbett National Park was established in 1936 and is India's first national park. It is known for its rich wildlife, including tigers, elephants, deer and numerous bird species.

Why Visit Uttarakhand?

  • Scenic Himalayan landscapes
  • Ancient temples and pilgrimage destinations
  • Hill stations and peaceful mountain towns
  • River rafting and adventure activities
  • Skiing and snow experiences
  • Wildlife safaris and birdwatching
  • Traditional Himalayan culture and cuisine
  • Trekking and camping opportunities

fullDescription.en: Mysuru, formerly known as Mysore, is one of South India's most elegant heritage destinations. The city is especially vibrant during the annual Dasara celebrations.

fullDescription.es: Hampi es uno de los paisajes arqueológicos y culturales más extraordinarios de India. Antigua capital del poderoso Imperio Vijayanagara, la región está llena de templos monumentales, complejos reales, antiguos mercados y estructuras de piedra rodeadas de enormes formaciones de granito y el río Tungabhadra. El templo Virupaksha, el templo Vittala y el Stone Chariot son algunas de sus principales atracciones.
fullDescription.en: Hampi is one of India's most extraordinary archaeological and cultural landscapes. Once the capital of the powerful Vijayanagara Empire, the region is filled with monumental temples, royal complexes, ancient markets and stone structures spread across a dramatic landscape of granite boulders and the Tungabhadra River. The Virupaksha Temple, Vittala Temple and Stone Chariot are among its most famous attractions. Hampi is ideal for history lovers, photographers, architecture enthusiasts and adventure-minded travellers.

Discover Gujarat – Heritage, Spirituality, Wildlife and the Rann

Gujarat is one of India's most diverse tourism destinations, combining ancient archaeological sites, historic cities, sacred pilgrimage centres, wildlife habitats, desert landscapes and a long coastline. The state offers experiences ranging from heritage walks and temple visits to wildlife safaris and desert excursions.

Ahmedabad is a major cultural and heritage destination and is recognised as India's first UNESCO World Heritage City. Gujarat's heritage attractions also include the historic stepwell of Rani ki Vav, the Sun Temple at Modhera, Champaner-Pavagadh and ancient sites connected with the Indus Valley civilisation.

Spiritual Gujarat

Gujarat has several important pilgrimage destinations. Dwarka is associated with Lord Krishna, while Somnath is home to the famous Somnath Temple, traditionally counted among the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva.

Wildlife and Nature

Gir National Park is internationally known for the Asiatic lion. The state also has other protected landscapes including Velavadar Blackbuck National Park, Marine National Park and the Little Rann of Kutch, where visitors can experience wildlife and distinctive ecosystems.

Rann of Kutch

The Great Rann of Kutch is one of Gujarat's most distinctive landscapes. Its vast white salt desert, traditional crafts, cultural experiences and seasonal festivals make the Kutch region an important tourism destination. Gujarat Tourism also highlights the Rann of Kutch and Kutch's forts, palaces, museums and pilgrimage sites.

Beaches and Coastal Experiences

Gujarat's coastline provides opportunities to explore beaches, marine landscapes and coastal pilgrimage destinations. Shivrajpur Beach near Dwarka is among the state's highlighted coastal attractions.

Festivals and Culture

Gujarat is famous for cultural celebrations such as Navratri and the International Kite Festival. Traditional handicrafts, textiles, folk music, dance and Gujarati cuisine add to the state's cultural identity.

Why Visit Gujarat?

  • UNESCO heritage and historic architecture
  • Ancient temples and pilgrimage sites
  • Great Rann of Kutch
  • Asiatic lion safari in Gir
  • Statue of Unity
  • Beautiful beaches and coastal landscapes
  • Traditional Gujarati cuisine
  • Colourful Navratri celebrations
  • Handicrafts and textile traditions
  • Indus Valley archaeological sites

overview.en:
Discover Punjab – The Land of Heritage, Faith and Flavours

Punjab is a culturally rich destination in northern India where history, spirituality, agriculture, music, food and traditional celebrations come together. The state has a strong connection with Sikh history and is home to some of the most important Sikh religious and historical sites in India.

Amritsar is the most prominent tourism destination in Punjab, attracting visitors to the Golden Temple, Jallianwala Bagh and the Wagah-Attari border. Patiala is known for its royal heritage and magnificent palaces, while Ludhiana represents the state's modern commercial and industrial character. Jalandhar combines religious heritage, historic landmarks and contemporary city life.

Spiritual Heritage

Punjab is deeply connected with Sikh history and traditions. Gurdwaras across the state provide opportunities to experience Sikh architecture, spirituality, community service and cultural traditions.

History and Heritage

The state has witnessed important events in Indian history, particularly during the Sikh Empire and the Indian freedom movement. Historical monuments and museums across Punjab allow travellers to explore these chapters of the past.

Punjab Cuisine

Punjabi cuisine is one of the most recognisable regional cuisines of India. Visitors can enjoy dishes such as Amritsari Kulcha, Sarson da Saag, Makki di Roti, Chole Bhature, Lassi and traditional Punjabi sweets.

Why Visit Punjab?

  • Golden Temple and Sikh heritage
  • Historic monuments and museums
  • Royal palaces and forts
  • Traditional Punjabi cuisine
  • Colourful festivals and cultural traditions
  • Historic sites associated with India's freedom movement
  • Rural landscapes and agricultural experiences
  • Traditional music, dance and hospitality

overview.en:
Discover Andaman & Nicobar Islands – India's Tropical Island Paradise

The Andaman & Nicobar Islands form a remarkable group of islands in the Bay of Bengal and are among India's most distinctive travel destinations. The islands combine tropical beaches, dense forests, coral reefs, marine biodiversity, historical monuments and opportunities for adventure.

The destination offers very different experiences across its islands. Sri Vijaya Puram provides the historical and administrative gateway to the islands, with attractions such as Cellular Jail, museums, Corbyn's Cove and access to nearby islands. Swaraj Dweep is famous for its beautiful beaches, especially Radhanagar Beach, and marine activities such as snorkeling and scuba diving.

Shaheed Dweep provides a quieter island experience with beaches, coral formations and the famous Natural Bridge. Baratang is known for mangrove landscapes, limestone caves and mud volcanoes, while Rangat, Mayabunder and Diglipur offer opportunities to explore the less-developed natural landscapes of Middle and North Andaman.

Beaches & Tropical Landscapes

The islands are known for their beautiful beaches, clear waters, tropical vegetation and spectacular sunsets. Radhanagar Beach, Bharatpur Beach, Lakshmanpur Beach, Kalipur Beach, Wandoor Beach and several other coastal locations provide different experiences ranging from relaxation to nature exploration.

Marine Life & Coral Reefs

Andaman is particularly attractive to travellers interested in marine ecosystems. Snorkeling, scuba diving, glass-bottom boat rides and other marine experiences provide opportunities to observe coral reefs and underwater environments. The official tourism portal lists scuba diving, snorkeling, sea walks, glass-bottom boat rides, kayaking, parasailing and several other water-based activities.

Historical Heritage

The islands also have an important place in India's modern history. Cellular Jail in Sri Vijaya Puram is one of the most significant historical landmarks of the region and is preserved as a national memorial connected with India's freedom struggle.

Colonial History

Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep, formerly known as Ross Island, contains remains of British-era buildings, churches, offices and other structures. The island combines colonial ruins with tropical vegetation and coastal scenery.

Adventure Tourism

  • Scuba Diving
  • Snorkeling
  • Sea Walking
  • Kayaking
  • Parasailing
  • Jet Skiing
  • Glass-Bottom Boat Rides
  • Trekking
  • Bird Watching
  • Game Fishing
  • Camping
  • Stargazing

Eco-Tourism

Several parts of Andaman & Nicobar provide opportunities to experience mangrove ecosystems, tropical forests, beaches and wildlife habitats. The official tourism itineraries include mangrove walks, eco-parks, bird watching, nature trails and island excursions.

Island Hopping

One of the best ways to experience Andaman is to combine multiple islands in one journey. Sri Vijaya Puram, Swaraj Dweep, Shaheed Dweep, Baratang and North Andaman can offer distinctly different experiences.

Connectivity

Veer Savarkar International Airport in Sri Vijaya Puram is the principal air gateway to the islands. Inter-island ferry services connect populated islands and tourist destinations, while other boat services operate on selected routes. The official tourism portal also lists helicopter services to several destinations.
overview.es:
Descubre las Islas Andamán y Nicobar – El Paraíso Tropical de la India

Las Islas Andamán y Nicobar forman un extraordinario conjunto de islas en la Bahía de Bengala y constituyen uno de los destinos turísticos más singulares de la India. El archipiélago combina playas tropicales, bosques densos, arrecifes de coral, biodiversidad marina, monumentos históricos y numerosas experiencias de aventura.

Cada isla ofrece una experiencia diferente. Sri Vijaya Puram funciona como puerta de entrada histórica y administrativa y cuenta con lugares como Cellular Jail, museos, Corbyn's Cove y acceso a varias islas cercanas. Swaraj Dweep es famoso por sus playas, especialmente Radhanagar Beach, además de sus actividades marinas.

Shaheed Dweep ofrece una experiencia insular más tranquila, con playas, formaciones de coral y el famoso Natural Bridge. Baratang destaca por sus manglares, cuevas de piedra caliza y volcanes de lodo, mientras que Rangat, Mayabunder y Diglipur permiten descubrir paisajes naturales menos urbanizados.

Playas y Paisajes Tropicales

Las islas son conocidas por sus playas, aguas transparentes, vegetación tropical y espectaculares atardeceres. Radhanagar Beach, Bharatpur Beach, Lakshmanpur Beach, Kalipur Beach y Wandoor Beach ofrecen diferentes experiencias para los viajeros.

Vida Marina y Arrecifes

Andamán es especialmente atractivo para los viajeros interesados en ecosistemas marinos. El snorkel, el buceo, los paseos en barcos con fondo de cristal y otras actividades permiten descubrir los arrecifes y ambientes submarinos.

Patrimonio Histórico

Cellular Jail en Sri Vijaya Puram es uno de los monumentos históricos más importantes de las islas y está relacionado con la historia de la lucha por la independencia de la India. Actualmente está preservado como monumento nacional.

Historia Colonial

Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep, anteriormente conocido como Ross Island, conserva restos de edificios británicos, iglesias y oficinas históricas, rodeados por vegetación tropical y paisajes costeros.

The destination offers very different experiences across its islands. Sri Vijaya Puram provides the historical and administrative gateway to the islands, with attractions such as Cellular Jail, museums, Corbyn's Cove and access to nearby islands. Swaraj Dweep is famous for its beautiful beaches, especially Radhanagar Beach, and marine activities such as snorkeling and scuba diving.

Shaheed Dweep provides a quieter island experience with beaches, coral formations and the famous Natural Bridge. Baratang is known for mangrove landscapes, limestone caves and mud volcanoes, while Rangat, Mayabunder and Diglipur offer opportunities to explore the less-developed natural landscapes of Middle and North Andaman.

Beaches & Tropical Landscapes

The islands are known for their beautiful beaches, clear waters, tropical vegetation and spectacular sunsets. Radhanagar Beach, Bharatpur Beach, Lakshmanpur Beach, Kalipur Beach, Wandoor Beach and several other coastal locations provide different experiences ranging from relaxation to nature exploration.

Marine Life & Coral Reefs

Andaman is particularly attractive to travellers interested in marine ecosystems. Snorkeling, scuba diving, glass-bottom boat rides and other marine experiences provide opportunities to observe coral reefs and underwater environments. The official tourism portal lists scuba diving, snorkeling, sea walks, glass-bottom boat rides, kayaking, parasailing and several other water-based activities.

Historical Heritage

The islands also have an important place in India's modern history. Cellular Jail in Sri Vijaya Puram is one of the most significant historical landmarks of the region and is preserved as a national memorial connected with India's freedom struggle.

Colonial History

Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep, formerly known as Ross Island, contains remains of British-era buildings, churches, offices and other structures. The island combines colonial ruins with tropical vegetation and coastal scenery.

overview.en:
Discover West Bengal – A Journey from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal

West Bengal offers an extraordinary variety of travel experiences within one state. Its landscape changes dramatically from the snow-covered Himalayan region in the north to tea gardens, forests, river plains, historic towns, coastal beaches and the mangrove ecosystems of the Sundarbans in the south. The official West Bengal Tourism Department highlights mountain tourism, eco-tourism, tea tourism, cultural tourism, heritage tourism, coastal tourism, wildlife tourism, religious tourism and river cruises as major tourism experiences across the state.

Himalayan West Bengal

The northern districts offer spectacular mountain landscapes, tea estates, forests, valleys and views of Himalayan peaks. Darjeeling is one of the state's most recognizable hill destinations, while Kalimpong provides a quieter hill-town experience surrounded by mountains and river valleys.

Tea Tourism

Tea is an important part of the tourism identity of North Bengal. Visitors can explore tea gardens, learn about tea cultivation, enjoy mountain scenery and experience the distinctive atmosphere of tea-estate regions. West Bengal Tourism specifically promotes tea tourism as a tourism category.

Heritage & History

West Bengal has a deep historical legacy reflected in colonial buildings, old palaces, temples, museums, churches, mosques and heritage towns. Kolkata, Murshidabad and Bishnupur are particularly valuable for travellers interested in architecture, history and cultural heritage.

Culture & Festivals

Bengali culture is strongly associated with literature, music, theatre, visual arts, handicrafts and festivals. Durga Puja is one of the most prominent cultural celebrations of the state, while Santiniketan represents an important centre of art, education and cultural heritage. West Bengal Tourism identifies cultural tourism and Durga Puja as major tourism themes.

Wildlife & Nature

The state contains a wide range of ecosystems, including Himalayan forests, Dooars grasslands, riverine landscapes and the mangrove forests of the Sundarbans. Wildlife experiences can include elephants, rhinoceroses, leopards, birds and the Royal Bengal Tiger in the Sundarbans ecosystem.

Beaches

The Bay of Bengal coastline provides destinations such as Digha, Mandarmani, Bakkhali and Gangasagar. These destinations provide beach walks, sunsets, coastal scenery and relaxed seaside holidays. The official tourism portal identifies coastal tourism as a major category.

Food Tourism

West Bengal is also an important destination for food lovers. Bengali cuisine is known for rice-based meals, fish preparations, mustard-based flavours, sweets and street food. Kolkata in particular is promoted by West Bengal Tourism as a food destination.

Playas

Digha, Mandarmani, Bakkhali y Gangasagar ofrecen experiencias costeras, paseos junto al mar y paisajes al atardecer.

La gastronomía bengalí es conocida por el pescado, el arroz, la mostaza, los sabores tradicionales y sus famosos dulces. Kolkata es especialmente conocida por su cultura gastronómica.

A cultura bengali está fortemente ligada à literatura, música, teatro, arte e artesanato. Durga Puja é uma das celebrações culturais mais importantes do estado.

Natureza e Vida Selvagem

O estado possui diferentes ecossistemas, desde florestas do Himalaia até as pradarias de Dooars e os manguezais de Sundarbans. Sundarbans é conhecido pelo tigre-de-bengala e por seu extraordinário ecossistema de manguezais.

Praias

Digha, Mandarmani, Bakkhali e Gangasagar oferecem experiências costeiras, caminhadas à beira-mar e belas paisagens ao pôr do sol.

Gastronomia

A culinária bengali é conhecida pelo peixe, arroz, mostarda, sabores tradicionais e doces famosos. Kolkata é especialmente conhecida por sua cultura gastronômica.

Descubre Delhi – Donde el Pasado de la India se Encuentra con la Modernidad

Delhi es una ciudad con una extraordinaria profundidad histórica y una enorme diversidad cultural. Durante siglos, la región estuvo relacionada con poderosos reinos, imperios, diferentes tradiciones arquitectónicas y cambios políticos. Actualmente, Delhi combina este impresionante patrimonio con modernas infraestructuras, barrios contemporáneos, zonas comerciales, centros empresariales y una vibrante cultura gastronómica.

La ciudad permite descubrir diferentes aspectos de la India en un solo destino. Old Delhi ofrece una experiencia relacionada con la histórica Shahjahanabad a través del Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Chandni Chowk, mercados tradicionales y comida callejera. New Delhi, por otro lado, presenta amplias avenidas, edificios gubernamentales monumentales, museos, monumentos y espacios urbanos planificados.

Patrimonio Mundial y Monumentos Históricos

Delhi alberga tres importantes monumentos declarados Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO: Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb y Red Fort.

Old Delhi y Patrimonio Mogol

Old Delhi es una de las zonas con mayor personalidad de la capital. Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Chandni Chowk, antiguos edificios religiosos, havelis y mercados tradicionales forman un paisaje cultural único.

New Delhi y Arquitectura Colonial

La zona de New Delhi presenta importantes lugares relacionados con la historia política moderna de la India, incluyendo Rashtrapati Bhavan, India Gate, avenidas monumentales, museos y memoriales.

Gastronomía

La gastronomía forma parte esencial de la experiencia de Delhi. La ciudad es conocida por la cocina del norte de la India, especialidades mogoles, comida callejera, chaat, kebabs, parathas y dulces tradicionales.
overview.en:
Discover Delhi – Where India's Past Meets Its Modern Spirit

Delhi is a city of extraordinary historical depth and cultural diversity. For centuries, the region has been associated with powerful kingdoms, empires, architectural movements and changing political centres. Today, Delhi combines this remarkable heritage with modern infrastructure, contemporary neighbourhoods, shopping districts, business centres and a vibrant food culture.

The city offers travellers an opportunity to explore several different sides of India within a single destination. Old Delhi introduces visitors to the atmosphere of historic Shahjahanabad through the Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Chandni Chowk, traditional markets and famous street food. New Delhi, on the other hand, showcases broad avenues, monumental government buildings, museums, memorials and planned urban spaces.

World Heritage & Historical Monuments

Delhi is home to three major UNESCO World Heritage monuments: Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb and the Red Fort. These monuments represent different periods of Delhi's architectural and political history.

Old Delhi & Mughal Heritage

Old Delhi is one of the most atmospheric parts of the capital. The Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Chandni Chowk, historic religious buildings, old havelis and traditional markets create a distinctive cultural landscape.

New Delhi & Colonial Architecture

The New Delhi area features important landmarks associated with India's modern political history, including Rashtrapati Bhavan, India Gate, government avenues, museums and memorials.

Religious Diversity

Delhi reflects India's diverse religious traditions through Hindu temples, Sikh gurdwaras, mosques, churches, Jain temples and Buddhist sites.

Markets & Shopping

Delhi is also a major shopping destination. Visitors can explore traditional markets, handicraft centres, modern shopping districts, bazaars and cultural marketplaces.

Food & Culinary Experiences

Food is an important part of experiencing Delhi. The city is particularly known for North Indian and Mughlai cuisine, street food, chaat, kebabs, parathas, sweets and a wide range of regional Indian dishes.
